service: FDG PET scan of the brain for differential diagnosis of frontotemporal dementia versus Alzheimer's disease
vignette: 68-year-old man diagnosed with dementia two months ago. His wife reports that 14 months ago he began making inappropriate comments to strangers and lost the ability to manage the household finances, followed by forgetfulness. A behavioral neurologist who specializes in dementia performed a comprehensive evaluation: history from the patient and his wife including activities of daily living, physical and neurological examination, Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores of 24 fourteen months ago and 19 now (formal documentation of decline over 14 months), neuropsychological testing showing both executive and memory deficits, normal B12 and thyroid-stimulating hormone, and a brain MRI with generalized atrophy and no stroke or mass. He meets diagnostic criteria for both Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia; the neurologist documents that early disinhibition makes FTD a suspected alternative cause, that the evaluation did not establish a specific cause, and that FDG PET is expected to distinguish FTD from AD and guide treatment. He has never had a brain SPECT or PET scan. The record documents the date of symptom onset, the clinical syndrome (mild dementia), the cognitive scores, the presumptive cause (uncertain AD), the neuropsychological results, the MRI report, the laboratory results, and his three prescribed medications by name. The scan will be performed at a hospital nuclear medicine department with all necessary accreditation and read by a nuclear medicine physician experienced in interpreting dementia PET scans.
rationale_note: All B.1 conditions met and all record items present; no prior SPECT or PET.

vignette: 59-year-old woman with treated hypertension, diagnosed with dementia last month. Her husband reports progressive word-finding difficulty and poor planning, followed by forgetfulness. She meets diagnostic criteria for both Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia; the psychiatrist documents that early language difficulty raises suspicion of FTD, that the cause remains uncertain after evaluation, and that FDG PET is expected to clarify FTD versus AD and guide treatment. She has had no prior brain SPECT or PET. The record contains the onset date, clinical syndrome (mild dementia), MMSE scores, presumptive cause (possible AD), neuropsychological results, CT report, laboratory results, and the names of her two medications. The scan will be done at an imaging center with all accreditation required to operate nuclear medicine equipment and read by a neuroradiologist experienced with dementia PET.
rationale_note: Boundary: cognitive decline documented over exactly 6 months ('at least 6 months'). Early-onset age and treated hypertension are distractors.

The neurologist documents that FTD is suspected as an alternative cause, that the specific cause remains uncertain, and that a new FDG PET is expected to clarify FTD versus AD and guide treatment. The scan will be performed at an accredited hospital nuclear medicine department and read by an experienced nuclear medicine physician.
rationale_note: Repeat exception: prior FDG PET 15 months ago was inconclusive, there is an important change in severity, diagnosis remains uncertain, and more than one year has passed.

An FDG PET is requested to confirm the Alzheimer's diagnosis before starting a new medication. She has had no prior brain SPECT or PET. The record contains all of the listed documentation elements. The scan would be performed at an accredited nuclear medicine facility and read by an experienced nuclear medicine physician.
rationale_note: Clinically typical probable AD with no features suggesting FTD; PET requested only to confirm AD, which is a non-covered use.

service: FDG PET scan of the brain for differential diagnosis of frontotemporal dementia versus Alzheimer's disease
vignette: 74-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment diagnosed 8 months ago; he remains fully independent in activities of daily living and does not meet criteria for dementia. rationale_note: Mild cognitive impairment, not dementia meeting AD and FTD criteria; outside B.1, FDG PET is covered only in an approved clinical trial, and he is not enrolled in one.
